summary: Complete repository maintenance updated Chromium and installed its simdutf dependency.

Created a private read-only root recovery snapshot and retained the prior signed browser package. Refreshed package databases and ordinary desktop caches. Protected configuration, drivers, jobs and timer policy remained unchanged.
tests: Before and after: package database consistency passed. Before: Chromium file check and executable version passed. After: Chromium 276 files and simdutf 85 files checked with no alterations; executable version confirmed; separate update checker reported no pending updates. Inventory diff contained only these two packages. All 43 protected file hashes and modes and repository list remained unchanged. Snapshot read-only property verified. Final package-path and configuration review completed; no application code changes. GUI, gaming and performance tests were not run.
rollback: Prior signed Chromium package retained for a dependency-checked targeted rollback only if a regression is confirmed; new dependency can remain installed. Private read-only root snapshot retained as recovery source; nested subvolumes are excluded. No rollback performed because transaction and checks passed. Do not restore unrelated later data or reboot automatically.
problem: Pre-existing custom integration compatibility service remains failed because receipt acceptance and native proof requirements were not met. Current XFCE/LightDM differs from the recorded KDE/SDDM preference. Installed libclc is newer than the repository candidate.
solution: Package update succeeded. Integration report checksum verified and a local proposal retained for isolated receipt tests and capability-complete validation. Jobs, acceptance criteria and graphical session were preserved. Desktop transition requires an interactive reconciliation. No libclc downgrade performed.
reproduction: Read-only inspection of the existing custom integration state and prior validation report confirmed needs_attention; integration tests and jobs were not rerun. Installed package and service inventory confirmed the desktop divergence. These are local integration observations, not a demonstrated distribution defect.
